headline: MMDA Suspends Number Coding From 10:30 AM as Habagat Rains Persist
seoTitle: MMDA Suspends Number Coding on August 14 Amid Habagat Rains
seoDescription: The MMDA suspended Metro Manila's expanded number coding scheme from 10:30 a.m. on August 14 as continuous Habagat rain affected the capital region.
deck: The expanded number coding scheme was suspended from 10:30 a.m. Friday as continuous monsoon rain affected Metro Manila.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority suspended the expanded number coding scheme effective 10:30 a.m. on Friday, August 14, because of continuous rainfall associated with the southwest monsoon.
The suspension removed the remaining number-coding restriction for the day. Motorists still had to account for flooding and changing road conditions across parts of Metro Manila.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The suspension came as PAGASA rainfall warnings covered Metro Manila and nearby provinces. GMA News reported that the MMDA was monitoring several flooded road sections in Quezon City, Valenzuela and Manila on Friday morning.
This report does not repeat the bulletin's broader claims about emergency deployments or local government directives because those details were not established by the cited MMDA suspension report.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The change directly affected motorists who would otherwise have faced the Friday evening coding window. It did not mean all roads were clear or safe: commuters still needed current flood and traffic information before traveling.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Motorists should follow MMDA traffic and flood-monitoring advisories and local government instructions. Number-coding enforcement returns according to the agency's subsequent official announcements.
